messages:
Alex: FYI customer (NexHealth) opened an escalation — streaming responses showing very slow first payload (TTFB) vs non-streamed total time is fine. p95 TTFB ~700ms up from ~120ms last week. :warning:
Maria: Can you paste their minimal repro? SDK? region?
Alex: Using JS SDK v2.3.1 -> calls Redwood /v1/stream with stream=true. Region: us-west-2. Example curl they used:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-lite-7b","input":"summarize: ...","stream":true}' \\n  --http2 \\
  --no-buffer
```
Alex: Customer says if they switch to non-streaming endpoint the total latency stays ~450ms, but streaming first chunk often delayed 600-900ms then chunks stream fast after.
Kevin: That pattern smells like chunk coalescing / flush window. Do we have per-tenant coalesce overrides?
Olivia: Alertbot just fired a spike on stream_first_byte_latency_p95 for us-west-2 around 2024-11-06 14:12 UTC (inc-id: INC-4491). @Kevin can you check proxy and runtime traces?
alertbot: [ALERT] stream_first_byte_latency_p95 (us-west-2) crossed 500ms at 2024-11-06T14:12:08Z — link: https://dash.redwood.ai/alerts/INC-4491
Kevin: Looking at proxy logs for that timeframe — I see a lot of responses with header `x-coalesce=true` and `flush_window_ms=120`. Sample runtime trace snippet:
```
[t=2024-11-06T14:12:08Z] request_id=req_9a3c flush_delay=118ms coalesce=true path=/v1/stream model=redwood-lite-7b
[t=2024-11-06T14:12:08Z] request_id=req_9a3c kvcache_hit=false token_count=6
```
Kevin: Those flush_window_ms values are higher than our default 20ms. Looks like tenant override or a workload suggestion applied. Maria: Is this a global rollout of a coalesce policy or tenant-specific?
Alex: NexHealth is on a managed tenant plan but I don't see them in the recent rollout list. I captured their full request headers and route config and shared in the support ticket.
Maria: Quick repro I ran against a local canary route — toggling `coalesce` off drops TTFB from ~650ms -> ~90ms on short outputs. Repro steps: exact same payload, call stream endpoint, compare header `x-coalesce`.
Kevin: Good test. Two paths: 1) short-term mitigation = set `coalesce=false` or lower `flush_window_ms` for that tenant/route; 2) longer = investigate why autosuggester bumped the window (maybe due to batching heuristics for model variants).
Olivia: Ops: can we apply tenant override for NexHealth to set `flush_window_ms=10` and `coalesce=false` as a P1 temp fix? We'll monitor p95/p99 for 30m then rollback if downstream cost spike.
Kevin: I'll push a per-tenant config change now to canary -> NexHealth only. Patch: `route.overrides.nexhealth = { coalesce: false, flush_window_ms: 10 }`. Rolling out to canary (1% traffic) first.
Maria: While Kevin does that, Alex can you ask customer to try `--no-buffer` and confirm? Also ask them to capture TCP timings (ttfb) from curl `-w '%{time_starttransfer}\n'` so we have client-side numbers.
Alex: Yep, asked them. They returned curl starttransfer=0.72s (consistent). Also provided a short recording of the issue.
Kevin: Canary applied at 14:31 UTC to 1% — collecting metrics. If p95 drops for the canary group, we can expand.
alertbot: [INFO] config_change route.overrides.nexhealth applied to canary at 2024-11-06T14:31:05Z by Kevin
Olivia: Important — track cost delta. Disabling coalesce increases token compute by ~3-8% on short-turn workloads. Set temporary budget guard.
Kevin: Canary p95 for first byte (canary) after change: 92ms. Control still ~680ms. Good signal. Pushing to 25% now.
Maria: Nice. Also create a short regression eval to run nightly against synthetic short prompts to catch future autosuggester regressions.
Alex: Customer confirmed improvement after we moved them to the override on their tenant — TTFB ~80-120ms now. They're happy with the immediate fix. They asked for a permanent plan.
Kevin: For permanent: need to audit autosuggester heuristics. There's a case where batching optimizer increases flush_window for presumed throughput gains; it overshot for short-turn interactive workload. I'll open a tracking ticket and propose adding a workload classifier to avoid applying the heuristic to low-token-turns.
Maria: Filing follow-up: ACTIONS — (1) Kevin opens runtime ticket with traces + root cause (2) DevEx adds nightly regression for TTFB on short prompts (3) Support documents tenant override steps; communicate to NexHealth and close ticket once docs shared.
Alex: I'll send the customer the remediation steps and note we'll follow up on a permanent fix. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Olivia: Good triage. Marking incident INC-4491 resolved after monitoring window.
alertbot: [RESOLVED] INC-4491 closed at 2024-11-06T15:05:12Z
Alex: Closing thread — will follow up with updates from Kevin's runtime ticket.
